provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Colour mixing 1
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify yellow and red colours.
The pupils should be able to mix yellow and red to make orange.
Introduction:
We have learned about different colours.
Today we will mix two colours to make a new one.
Content:
Yellow and red are primary colours.
When we mix yellow and red paint we get orange.
We use a brush to mix the colours.
Class activity:
Give each pupil yellow and red paint.
Let them mix the paints to make orange.
Evaluation questions:
What colour do we get when we mix yellow and red?
Show me the yellow paint.
Show me the red paint.
Summary:
We can mix two colours to make a new colour.

topics.title: Colour mixing 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify blue and yellow colours.
The pupils should be able to mix blue and yellow to make green.
Introduction:
We learned how to mix yellow and red to make orange.
Today we will mix blue and yellow to make green.
Content:
Blue and yellow are primary colours.
When we mix blue and yellow paint we get green.
Green is the colour of many plants in Nigeria.
Class activity:
Give each pupil blue and yellow paint.
Let them mix the paints to make green.
Then paint a green tree on paper.
Evaluation questions:
What colour do we get when we mix blue and yellow?
What colour is the leaf of a mango tree?
Show me the blue paint.
Summary:
We can mix blue and yellow to make green colour.

topics.title: Drawing myself
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw the basic parts of the body.
The pupils should be able to add facial features to their drawing.
Introduction:
We have been making art with paints and leaves.
Today we will draw ourselves on paper.
Content:
We all have a head, hands and legs.
We also have eyes, nose and mouth.
We can draw these parts to make our picture.
Class activity:
Give each pupil a paper and crayon.
Let them draw their head, hands and legs.
Then add eyes and a smile to their face.
Evaluation questions:
What parts of your body did you draw?
Show me your drawing of your eyes.
What colour is your hair?
Summary:
We can draw ourselves by drawing our body parts.

topics.title: Drawing my family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw people of different sizes.
The pupils should be able to identify family members in their drawing.
Introduction:
We learned to draw ourselves last week.
Today we will draw our family members.
Content:
Family members can be big or small.
Big people are like our father and mother.
Small people are like our baby brother or sister.
Class activity:
Give each pupil a paper and crayon.
Let them draw big people and small people.
Help them name who is who in their drawing.
Evaluation questions:
Who is the biggest person in your family?
Who is the smallest person in your family?
Draw your father on the board.
Summary:
We can draw our family by showing their different sizes.

topics.title: Leaf printing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different leaf shapes.
The pupils should be able to make prints using leaves.
Introduction:
We have seen many different leaves in our environment.
Today we will use leaves to make art prints.
Content:
Leaves have different shapes and sizes.
Some leaves have lines on them.
We can use paint to make prints of leaves.
Class activity:
Give each pupil different leaves and paint.
Let them paint one side of a leaf.
Then press the painted leaf on paper to make a print.
Evaluation questions:
What lines can you see on the leaf?
What shape is the leaf you used?
Show me how to make a leaf print.
Summary:
We can make beautiful prints using real leaves.

topics.title: Clay fruits
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mould clay into fruit shapes.
The pupils should be able to paint dried clay fruits.
Introduction:
We have seen many fruits in the market.
Today we will make fruits using clay.
Content:
Clay is soft material we can shape.
We can mould clay to make an orange shape.
We can also mould clay to make a banana shape.
Class activity:
Give each pupil clay and water.
Let them mould an orange and a banana.
When dry, let them paint their clay fruits.
Evaluation questions:
What fruit did you make with clay?
What colour is an orange?
What colour is a banana?
Summary:
We can mould clay to make different fruits.

topics.title: Cutting with help
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to cut along a straight line with help.
The pupils should be able to paste their cut strips.
Introduction:\ Cutting paper can be fun but needs care.
Today we will learn to cut with help.
Content:
Scissors are sharp tools for cutting paper.
We cut along a straight line to make strips.
After cutting we can paste the strips on paper.
Class activity:
Give each pupil paper and child-safe scissors.
Help them cut along a straight line to make strips.
Let them paste their cut strips on another paper.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use to cut paper?
Show me how to hold scissors safely.
What can you make with your cut strips?
Summary:
We can cut paper with help and paste to make art.

topics.title: String painting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use string to make paint designs.
The pupils should be able to create wavy patterns with string.
Introduction:
We have used brushes and leaves for painting.
Today we will use string to make designs.
Content:
String is a thin thread we can use for painting.
We dip string in paint and drag it on paper.
This makes wavy and interesting designs.
Class activity:
Give each pupil paper, paint and string.
Let them dip string in paint and drag on paper.
Encourage them to make different wavy designs.
Evaluation questions:
What did we use to make wavy designs?
Show me how to dip string in paint.
What shape did your string make?
Summary:
We can use string to make beautiful wavy paintings.

topics.title: Masks and faces
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to decorate a paper face.
The pupils should be able to add facial features to a mask.
Introduction:
We have drawn faces on paper before.
Today we will make and decorate paper masks.
Content:
A mask has eyes, nose and mouth.
We can use paper to make a face shape.
Then we add and decorate the facial features.
Class activity:
Give each pupil a paper cut-out of a face.
Let them add eyes, nose and mouth with crayons.
Encourage them to decorate their masks brightly.
Evaluation questions:
What parts does a face have?
Show me your decorated mask.
What colour did you use for the eyes?
Summary:
We can make masks by decorating paper faces.

topics.title: Art gallery walk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to appreciate others' artwork.
The pupils should be able to walk quietly and observe art.
Introduction:
We have made many beautiful artworks this term.
Today we will see everyone's art like in a gallery.
Content:
An art gallery is a place to see art.
We walk slowly and look at each picture.
We can clap for the artists to say thank you.
Class activity:
Arrange all pupils' artworks around the classroom.
Let them walk around quietly to see everyone's art.
Clap for each artist as you pass their artwork.
Evaluation questions:
What was your favourite artwork today?
Why do we walk quietly in the gallery?
Show me one beautiful drawing you saw.
Summary:
We can enjoy and appreciate art by walking in our art gallery.
